gap: No result ChatGPT got states the cost per hour of talk time or how many 8-hour workdays of calls one charge covers: Shokz OpenComm2 (2025) works out to $10.00 per talk hour and 2.0 workdays per charge, the OpenComm2 UC to $12.50, and the OpenMeet UC to $8.57 at Abt's $119.95, or 1.75 workdays (1.4 with its Busylight on).
standout_why: Openearclub's 'Best Bone Conduction Headphones With Mic' page (2026-09-21) lists the raw inputs (OpenComm2 UC $199.95, 16 h talk, 5 min = 2 h, 35 g) but does no maths. It gives no cost per talk hour, no workday count and no talk-minutes per charge-minute, and it has no OpenMeet UC. SoundGuys' OpenRun Pro 2 review gives 12 h, 30.3 g and 5 min = 150 min, but no talk time and no per-dollar figure. I could not read the cited RTINGS compare page, the OpenComm2 2025 review or the OpenMeet UC review: WebFetch got only the navigation shell, so I can't rule out per-hour figures there, though RTINGS reviews normally report measured hours, not cost per hour. ChatGPT's answers quote '16-hour talk time' and '12-hour battery' side by side as if they measured the same thing. They don't: the OpenRun models publish listening time only.
decides: This confirms the OpenComm2 (2025) at $159.95 as the value pick among boom-mic models: $10.00 per talk hour, and two full 8-hour days of calls per charge. The UC version costs $2.50 more per talk hour for the USB adapter, so it only makes sense for PC-first users. The OpenMeet UC, which ChatGPT never showed as a card, is cheapest per talk hour at Abt's $119.95. But it weighs 78 g against 35 g and lasts 11 h with the Busylight on, so it suits a desk headset more than all-day wear. The OpenRun Pro 2 and OpenRun Air 2 publish no talk time at all, so their 12 h and 10 h figures can't be set against the OpenComm's 16 h talk. A Dealectric page can say that plainly. The listed MOJAWA Run Plus is a music/sport model and was not costed.
